methodological_rigor.justification: Phase 2b randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (n=36 randomized, 26 in primary efficacy population). Appropriate sample size calculation (80% power for 47% difference). Rigorous blinding maintained with opaque coverings, computer-generated randomization with variable block sizes. Primary endpoint analysis using modified intention-to-treat with multiple imputation for missing data (fully conditional specification method). Appropriate statistical tests (Wald chi-squared for proportions). Subgroup analyses conducted for antibody status and disease onset timing.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Phase 2b RCT in generalized myasthenia gravis with clinically meaningful endpoints: 66.7% of patients achieved ≥5-point MGC improvement vs 27.3% placebo (P=0.047). Secondary outcomes show sustained benefit at 12 months with 83% maintaining response; 33% achieved MSE (MG-ADL≤1). Study enrolls treatment-refractory patients (40% on complement inhibitors, 33% prior FcRn inhibitors), strengthening clinical relevance. Single course of six weekly infusions provides durable effect without ongoing treatment.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive reporting of trial design, randomization procedures, blinding maintenance, and statistical methods. CONSORT diagram clearly shows participant flow. Baseline characteristics table well-presented. Multiple efficacy endpoints with standardized outcome measures (MGC, MG-ADL, QMG, MG-QoL-15r). Safety reporting includes AEs coded by CTCAE v5.0, laboratory parameters, and vital signs. Protocol amendments documented. Data availability statement references Nature Portfolio reporting summary but specific repository details limited.

novelty_literature.justification: First placebo-controlled RCT of mRNA-based CAR-T therapy in autoimmunity. Phase 2b trial with planned transition to phase 3, demonstrating clinical efficacy endpoint. MGC chosen as primary endpoint per MGFA Task Force recommendations, appropriate for future regulatory submissions. Transient CAR expression without lymphodepletion represents novel approach vs integrating CD19 CAR-T. Sustained clinical response after single infusion course addresses major unmet need in refractory MG.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear trial design, participant flow, and outcome reporting. Methods section comprehensive with appropriate statistical detail. Results systematically presented by primary and secondary endpoints with supporting tables. Long-term follow-up data (month 12) provided. Discussion contextualizes findings within MG management landscape and compares to other biologics (FcRn inhibitors, complement inhibitors). Figures and tables clearly labeled with appropriate statistical notation.

key_strengths: Rigorous phase 2b RCT with double-blind, placebo-controlled design demonstrating clinically meaningful efficacy (66.7% vs 27.3%, P=0.047) in generalized myasthenia gravis
Sustained clinical benefit at 12 months with 83% maintaining response and 33% achieving minimum symptom expression (MSE) after single course of six weekly infusions
Comprehensive safety profile without major adverse events; infusion-related reactions most common (80% Descartes-08 vs 56.3% placebo), managed with premedication
Enrollment of refractory patient population (40% on complement inhibitors, 33% prior FcRn inhibitors) strengthens clinical relevance and demonstrates efficacy in treatment-resistant disease

Well-designed blinding procedures (opaque coverings, computer-generated randomization with variable block sizes) and rigorous statistical analysis (multiple imputation for missing data, appropriate tests for proportions)
key_concerns: Relatively small sample size (n=26 primary efficacy population) limits generalizability; wide confidence intervals on responder difference (95% CI 0.01–0.77)
Unequal allocation between treatment groups (15 Descartes-08 vs 11 placebo in efficacy population) acknowledged as result of manufacturing failures and lack of stratification
Primary endpoint changed during trial from MG-ADL to MGC after enrollment of 44/50 participants and before database lock—post hoc change despite good intention to align with MGFA recommendations
Limited mechanistic detail in this outcomes paper; companion biomarker paper (PMC13004674) required for full understanding of mechanism

Comparison to historical placebo controls and prior phase 2a results rather than concurrent active comparator; cannot assess relative efficacy vs other emerging therapies (FcRn inhibitors, complement inhibitors)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid phase 2b RCT demonstrating clinical efficacy of novel mRNA CAR-T approach in refractory myasthenia gravis with durable benefit and acceptable safety. Appropriate for Tier 1 journals as proof-of-concept for new therapeutic class. Minor concerns about sample size and mid-trial endpoint change do not substantially diminish contribution.
